newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mulling tension-reducing measures in Korea.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mulling tension-reducing measures in Korea.

text.p: The United States plans to propose new ways to ease tensions between the two Koreas as part of a negotiating process that begins on Tuesday in New York, U.S. officials said on Friday.

The United States, China, South Korea and North Korea are to sit down for the first time together that day at Columbia University to work out the mundane details of when and where substantive peace talks will take place.

But once that is settled and the substantive negotiations begin -- expected in September -- confidence building measures between the two Koreas like exchanging military visits and providing advance notification of military manuevers are among the U.S. proposals to be advanced, officials said.
Other proposals are expected in the economic and political spheres as well, said a U.S. official who briefed reporters on the talks.

Although essentially "talks about talks," the New York meeting will mark the first time that North Korea sits down with the United States, South Korea and China after agreeing to join in four-party talks aimed at mapping a more enduring peace arrangement for the Korean peninsula.
The four countries were parties to the armistice -- now badly frayed -- that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.

It took more than a year to get the Stalinist regime, preoccupied with the famine facing North Korea and obtaining emergency food assistance from the United States and elsewhere, to participate in the peace effort.
The U.S. official said that "just because they (North Korea) may have very low expectations for these talks, the talks can succeed in spite of it."
"You can't rule out results before you begin," he said.

He cited as an example the 1994 landmark agreement under which North Korea agreed to freeze its nuclear programme in return for a U.S. commitment to provide $4.5 biillion in two new nuclear power reactors and oil supplies to meet Pyongyang's energy needs.
Doubts have been raised repeatedly about North Korea's commitment to that accord but so far the agreement is holding.
The main goal of next week's talks is to produce a specific date for substantive negotiations, the official said. The location and agenda will also be discussed.
Although the meeting is set only for one day -- Tuesday -- all sides expect it to run for several days, the official said.
